what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted unanimously to recommend that the Select Board and Town Manager consider hiring or looking into a grant writer; the vote is non-binding.
The committee held a public question-and-answer session on town revenue, Proposition 2 and a half and how an override works, amid proposed school cuts.
The town is no longer receiving the 40S smart growth reimbursement; the amount was stated as a figure over three hundred thousand.
Residents asked who sets the budget and tax rate, how an override could be started, and why the state grants were lost.
The committee skipped its reports and future topics to move to a second round of public comment.

why_it_matters: The loss of a state reimbursement takes a source of town revenue away, which makes a gap between the levy limit and the cost of services harder to close without cuts or an override.
Residents questioned how an override could reach the warrant and when the budget timeline lets them weigh in, so a vote on an override may be put to them.
watch_next: Whether the Select Board and Town Manager act on the grant writer recommendation, which has no binding force.
Whether an override question is placed on the town warrant, which the minutes do not decide.
